title: המשגר המתפצל

spec.palette: designed ramps, at most 5 steps each: steel 4, olive 5, band 2, flash 3, rubber 2, smoke 2, red 2, tag 2, mark 1

source: hand-placed pixels at 0 deg, every column (tools/art_host/weapons/cluster_px.py); rows turned RotSprite-style (Scale2x x3, nearest), stray pixels out, a 1 px outline; the mark upright in the overlay only
character:
WHO: a fat olive drum launcher: a six-chamber revolving cylinder the size of a paint can, a short flared barrel with
       a yellow-and-black hazard band, a flip-up leaf sight, a skeleton steel stock. One shell in, six surprises out.
  IDLE: the cylinder clicks round one chamber now and then, the sight leaf wobbles. FIRE: a big orange flash and a
        smoke puff from the flare, a heavy kick; at 18 the cylinder turns to the next chamber with a pump.
cell_note: a bigger cell than the contract's 64: it holds the weapon at every angle with its moving parts thrown out and the toss

equip.note: 24 ticks: up from the hip; at 10 the cylinder CHAMBERS (turns one step with a clack): ready

idle.note: 1 s loop: the leaf sight wobbles, the cylinder clicks round a step and back

fire.note: 42 ticks: tick 0 the shell (a big orange flash at the flare), the heavy kick back and up peaking at 3, smoke from the mouth; at 18 the PUMP: the cylinder turns to the next chamber and the next shell's nose shows: ready

empty.note: 12 ticks: the click on an empty chamber, a droop; at 6 he tosses it away in front of him

catch.note: the hand-off from the unarmed catch: it lands in his hands, the cylinder chambers, the sight flips up; the reveal from the last frame

aim_note: a frame's aim = degrees the weapon turns from its rest (the idle's first frame is 0), added to the body's aim; kick = [px along the barrel (negative = back), px up, degrees up]
mark: the made-in-Israel mark as a SMALL HANGING TAG (the Host 12.11: at most 9 x 11): an ivory luggage tag with the blue outline star 7 x 7 on a 3 px cord from under the barrel; upright in every row. In atlas_mark.png ONLY
mark_rect_note: per angle row, per column: [x, y, w, h] of the mark in the cell (the 9 x 11 tag, or the 11 x 11 roundel) and mark_star = the top-left pixel of the star (7 x 7 on the tag, 9 x 9 on a roundel); atlas_mark.png holds the mark alone in the same layout

events.chamber: the cylinder turns a chamber in (equip 10): a heavy clack
events.ready: the act is over on this frame's last tick
events.shot: the shell leaves the flare (fire 0): FX's smoking shell from `muzzle`
events.pump: the cylinder turns to the next chamber (fire 18): a clack-clack
events.click: the trigger on an empty chamber (empty 0)
events.toss: the spent launcher leaves his hand (empty 6)
events.reveal: RENDER fires the reveal from this pose

normal_note: by plane: every colour paints one plane of the weapon (top, front, underside ...), turned with the row; silhouette pixels face out along the edge; the upright mark faces the viewer

holds.note: THE SET'S OWN CARRY per hero body pose (the Host 12.11: a hero's face is never covered by his weapon in any pose). While the king plays one of these body animations with this weapon, draw the weapon at `aim` (degrees, the body's hand aim replaced) and its hand point moved by `offset` [x, y] px; the frame's own aim delta and kick still add. His port carry (aim 25-40) puts a long weapon across his chin and mouth; a low hip carry at -20 keeps the face and the crown clear (picture: art/weapons/host/previews/king_carry_long_weapons.png).

muzzle_note: the flare's mouth, per row and column: the shell starts here

glow.note: the launch flash's colours as drawn at the flare: orange, a white-yellow core

cells: the canopy flat on the floor
sprites.anchor: the cell's TOP-left at `at` (frame px; the sprite stands on the cell's bottom, centred)

catch.note: the weapon's side of the unarmed set's catch, on the same ticks and hand points as the shotgun's catch.json (the body is one builder's): frames 0-2 it comes down, 3 the catch (its grip lands on the hand), 3-4 what carried it lets go, 5-6 in the hands, 7-9 held up behind his head (layer back), the reveal from 9. Its carrier is the parachute: on the catch it folds, then lies on the floor.
